title.rendered: The Cursed Fig Tree | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 7

excerpt.rendered: By the next morning the fig tree Jesus had spoken to was dead from the roots up. Peter noticed. Jesus used the moment to teach the disciples something about the authority their own words would carry.

content.rendered:
By the next morning, the fig tree Jesus had spoken to the day before was dead from the roots up. Not pruned. Not withering. Dead. Peter noticed it as they walked past. Jesus used the moment to teach the disciples something about the authority their own words were about to carry.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, October 9, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 7

Today’s Scripture

“In response Jesus said to it, ‘Let no one eat fruit from you ever again.’ And His disciples heard it… Now in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. And Peter, remembering, said to Him, ‘Rabbi, look! The fig tree which You cursed has withered away.'”
Mark 11:14, 20-21 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

On the morning after the triumphal entry into Jerusalem, Jesus was walking from Bethany to the Temple with His disciples. He was hungry. In the distance He saw a fig tree in full leaf. In first-century Palestine, a fig tree with full foliage was expected to have early fruit as well, since the leaves and the first figs appeared together. Jesus went to the tree looking for figs. There were none. The tree was all leaves and no fruit. A picture of empty religion. A tree that advertised the presence of fruit without delivering any. Jesus spoke one sentence to the tree. “Let no one eat fruit from you ever again.” The disciples heard it. They walked on into Jerusalem. Jesus cleansed the Temple that day, overturning the tables of the money-changers and driving out those who had turned His Father’s house into a den of thieves. By evening they left Jerusalem again and spent the night in Bethany.

The next morning, as they walked past the same fig tree on their way back to the Temple, Peter noticed something that stopped him. “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which You cursed has withered away.” Not pruned. Not sick. Not browning. Dead. Dried up from the roots. In less than twenty-four hours, a healthy tree in full leaf had died in response to one sentence from the lips of Jesus. That is the scene behind the mountain-moving teaching we studied yesterday. Jesus did not teach the disciples about authoritative prayer in a classroom. He taught them standing in front of the dead tree His words had killed.

The Passion Translation renders the scene with the drama it carried: “They came back and passed by the fig tree Jesus had cursed. Peter remembered what Jesus had done, and he said, ‘Teacher! Look at the fig tree you cursed—it has already dried up and withered away!'” (Mark 11:20-21 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “In the morning, when they were passing along, they noticed that the fig tree was withered [completely] away to its roots” (Mark 11:20 AMPC). Completely. To its roots. Jesus’ words carried authority that extended into the invisible, into the cellular, into the root system of a healthy tree, and the whole tree died from the inside out.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Jesus spoke directly to the fig tree. Not about the tree. Not to the Father concerning the tree. To the tree itself. The format teaches the believer that spiritual authority is often exercised in direct speech to the thing itself, not in petition to God about the thing.

The Essence. The believer’s spoken word, when it carries the authority of Christ and the faith of a heart rooted in God, has effects in the invisible realm that produce visible results. Jesus demonstrated the principle with a tree so the disciples could not miss it. A spoken word of authority produced a visible, undeniable, physical result.

The Authority. The authority was not in the volume of Jesus’ voice. It was not in the elaborateness of the words. It was in the One who was speaking, and in the alignment of His words with the Father’s will. The tree was a picture of empty religion. The Father wanted it cursed. Jesus simply voiced the judgment. The believer carries the same kind of authority when the believer’s words align with the Father’s heart.

The Assurance. Jesus did not go back to check whether the tree had died. He walked on into Jerusalem. He spent the day cleansing the Temple. He went back to Bethany for the night. He did not revisit the site to monitor the result. The assurance was so complete that the result was never in doubt. Peter is the one who notices the withered tree the next day. Jesus had already moved on to the next assignment.

The Submission. Jesus’ authority was always submitted to the Father’s heart. He did not curse trees for sport. He did not kill plants for showmanship. He pronounced judgment on a tree that symbolised the empty, fruitless, performative religion the Temple establishment had become. The curse of the tree was the enacted parable of the Temple cleansing He performed the same afternoon. Authority always serves the Father’s purpose, never the believer’s ego.

The Result. A dead tree, visible from the Jerusalem road, standing as a parable for every disciple who walked past it in the weeks that followed. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, your words carry weight you may not have realised. Jesus did not perform the fig tree miracle to show off. He performed it to show you what your own words are capable of, when they are spoken in His name, aligned with His will, from a heart that does not doubt. Watch your mouth. The things you speak will come to pass.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Father, I thank You that the authority of Jesus flows through my words when they are aligned with Your heart. The same Spirit that empowered the words of Jesus empowers mine today.

Awareness. Make me aware today of the weight of my own words. Where I have been speaking death over my body, my family, my work, my future, forgive me, and let me retract those words now.

Declaration. I speak life. I speak faith. I speak the Father’s purposes. I speak Kingdom-aligned words today, in every room I walk into, over every situation I encounter.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My words carry the authority of Christ. I speak life, not death. I speak faith, not fear. I speak the Father’s heart over every circumstance. What I say in alignment with His will comes to pass.
